subject: Clarify: Which countries handle request processing and deletion lifecycle
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@novamed.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Quick Q - where exactly are my users' inputs processed?

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week — NovaMed is excited by the latency profile. Before procurement we need a short written Q&A for our security team. Can you confirm: which countries/process regions actually execute inference for requests routed through Redwood hosted API (primary + fallbacks)?

Specifically we need:
- A plain list of regions/countries where inference runs for hosted customers (including any transient hops).
- Which subprocessors (cloud providers, edge/CDN, monitoring, backups) may touch request payloads and in which countries they operate.
- Whether request payloads ever transit through or get stored in third countries outside the EU for EU customer traffic.
- The deletion/retention timeline and what evidence you can provide that data is wiped (e.g., tombstone + backup purge windows).

We'd like something short we can hand to procurement/legal; PDF or CSV is fine. Also let us know if you can do a 20-min call with our engineering and legal folks tomorrow.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Senior Security Engineer
NovaMed Health

---
Attachment: none

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q - where exactly are my users' inputs processed?

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Laura (solutions) and Marissa (customer success) so we can share both the short summary and the evidence pack. High-level answers below; Laura will follow up with the CSV + a short timeline for deletion/attestations.

Short answer (hosted API):
- Primary execution regions: US (us-east-1), EU (europe-west/ireland), APAC (asia-southeast1/singapore).
- Fallbacks: Our smart router may send requests to an adjacent region for capacity; we do not route EU traffic to non-EU regions except for short transient handoffs when a model variant is unavailable in-region (we document that in the routing policy).
- Subprocessors that may touch request payloads: cloud compute (AWS/GCP/Azure regional clusters), object storage for optional artifacts, CDN for model artifacts, monitoring/logging providers for operational telemetry, and backups (periodic snapshots). We provide a per-customer subprocessor roster and region map (attached).
- Cross-border transit & storage: For EU-region customers we aim to keep execution in EU; transient routing to a non-EU region only occurs under constrained-capacity fallback and is logged; we can provide an export of routing decisions for the deal period.
- Deletion timeline (hosted default): request payloads are ephemeral — KV/prefix caches default TTL: 6 hours; request logs are tombstoned within 30 days; backup snapshots and long-tail replicas retained up to 90 days and then purged. Dedicated/Private customers can contract tighter retention or customer-managed KMS.

Attachments: residency_matrix_v2.csv (per-subprocessor region map), SLA_draft_NovaMed_2026.pdf (SLA + retention excerpt). Laura — over to you for the evidence pack and legal notes.

If you'd like a 20-min call, Marissa can propose slots.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: residency_matrix_v2.csv (CSV), SLA_draft_NovaMed_2026.pdf (PDF)

On Mon, Jul 26, 2026 at 10:03 AM Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short answer (hosted API):
> - Primary execution regions: US (us-east-1), EU (europe-west/ireland), APAC (asia-southeast1/singapore).
> - Fallbacks: Our smart router may send requests to an adjacent region for capacity; we do not route EU traffic to non-EU regions except for short transient handoffs when a model variant is unavailable in-region (we document that in the routing policy).

Thanks Alex — that's a helpful summary. A couple of follow-ups we need from legal/infosec to close procurement: 
1) Can you provide a signed attestation or certificate that the routing fallback for EU traffic is only used under constrained-capacity events and is logged? We need an auditable statement.
2) For the subprocessors you listed, please confirm which of them have the technical ability to access plaintext request payloads (read access to storage, snapshot restore privileges, or logging ingestion points). A simple table: subprocessor | country | can-access-plaintext (yes/no) is perfect.
3) Is KMS customer-manageable for the EU tenant? If not, what controls prevent Redwood from decrypting content?
4) Exact deletion windows we can put in the contract: tombstone timing, backup purge timing, and log retention.

If you can provide the attestation + the subprocessor table and a short call with your solutions engineer (Laura) tomorrow at 11:00 CET, we can move this through legal quickly.

Thanks,
Nina Park
Sr. Counsel, Procurement
NovaMed Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@novamed.com>, Nina Park <nina.park@novamed.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-27T08:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q - where exactly are my users' inputs processed? — Evidence pack and answers

Hi Nina / Samir — Laura here. Per Alex's note I've attached the residency matrix (CSV) and a short SLA excerpt. Answers below are written so your legal and infosec teams can copy into procurement language.

1) Signed attestation / fallback logging
- We can provide a signed attestation stating: "For Redwood hosted EU tenants, execution will be routed to EU-designated execution venues by default. Non-EU routing for EU tenant traffic only occurs under constrained-capacity fallback events; each fallback is logged with timestamp, source region, destination region, and reason." We can attach that as a one-page addendum for the contract.

2) Subprocessor access table (summary) — full roster attached in residency_matrix_v2.csv (excerpt below):
- AWS EC2 (eu-west-1) | Ireland | can-access-plaintext: yes (compute processes requests while in-memory)
- GCP Compute (europe-west1) | Belgium/Netherlands | can-access-plaintext: yes (regional compute)
- Azure VM (westeurope) | Netherlands | can-access-plaintext: yes
- Object storage (S3/GCS/Blob) | region-specific | can-access-plaintext: depends on customer configuration; default: storage used for optional artifacts and model binaries only
- CDN/provider (edge caching) | global | can-access-plaintext: no (edge caches only host static model assets)
- Monitoring/logging vendor (ingestion pipeline) | US/EU | can-access-plaintext: no (ingestion receives metadata & traces; full request payloads are truncated by default)
- Backup snapshots (cloud provider managed) | region-specific with fallback copies | can-access-plaintext: yes (snapshots can be restored but access is restricted and audited)

Note: the attached CSV includes the contractual subprocessor list, country locations, and evidence of data processing agreements (DPA/SoAs). If you need a signed subprocessor attestation we can provide that as a separate exhibit.

3) KMS and encryption
- For Hosted customers we offer two options: (a) Redwood-managed keys (default) — keys stored in the cloud provider KMS and managed by Redwood; (b) Customer-managed keys (recommended for regulated customers) — bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS/CloudHSM or GCP KMS/HSM. When a customer elects customer-managed KMS, Redwood does not have key unwrap permissions and cannot decrypt customer ciphertext. We will add the KMS configuration option to the deal appendix.

4) Concrete deletion windows for contract language (hosted defaults; can be tightened for Dedicated/Private):
- Ephemeral inference caches (KV/prefix): TTL default = 6 hours; tombstoned immediately upon TTL expiry.
- Request logs (searchable/ingestion logs): tombstone marker within 30 days; records purged from primary indexes within 45 days.
- Backup snapshots & cold replicas: retention up to 90 days then scheduled purge; snapshot deletion is irreversible once completed.
- Audit/trace logs used for billing: retained for 365 days; exportable on request.

Evidence we can provide for procurement: signed fallback attestation, subprocessor roster CSV (attached), SOC 2 Type II report redacted excerpts, and a KMS configuration checklist.

Next steps: I can join a 20-min call tomorrow 11:00 CET to run through the attestation and the KMS options. Marissa — can you propose the meeting invite and include the artifact pack?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
